cards.title: Dossier acts from the mutation's own planner: offer, count, refusal (ADR 0107)
acceptance: every seeded table: table.acts.tidy.count === planNormalize(table.ids, ['trim_whitespace','lowercase_email']).length (today the button prints table.ids.length: 800 labelled vs 78 that would change, 46 of 46 tables overclaim) -> equal for all 46
run normalizeAction on one table's ids, rebuild the sheet -> that table's acts.tidy is {enabled:false, reason:'nothing_to_tidy'} with the REFUSAL sentence, not an enabled 'Tidy ... N rows' button

cards.body:
## Summary
The dossier decides what it offers from its own inline predicates, and the mutation decides what it accepts from another. They have drifted: the tidy act labels 800 rows across the 46 tables where 78 would change, and flagging stale rows (the reversible act) makes the gated delete vanish for good. Port ADR 0107 to tidycrm: one acts module, built server-side from the mutation's own planner, that every dossier control renders from.

## Description
`lib/acts.ts` (pure except for the planner it is handed) computes, per table, `{tidy, phone, flag, keep_both, merge, delete}`, each `{enabled, count, ids, reason?}` with one REFUSAL vocabulary. `lib/blocks/index.ts` attaches it to `BkTable.acts` while it already has every row in memory, using `planChanges` (lib/normalize.ts) so it adds no queries. The delete act targets stale rows flagged or not, which is exactly what deleteContacts already accepts. It stays behind arm and confirm, so no gate is weakened. `Gate.tsx` stops computing availability and reads `table.acts`. The parity test runs every seeded table through every act against the real mutations, each call rolled back, as hirelane's test/acts.test.ts does. This is registry technique hitl-approval/cosmetic-vs-enforced-threshold-invariant (two threshold tables kept by discipline alone) and law count-carries-predicate.

## Flow
- buildSheet -> per table, acts = actsFor(rows, pairs) via planChanges -> BkTable.acts
- Dossier -> Gate renders each control's disabled state, label count and refusal from acts
- person flags 5 stale rows -> sheet revalidates -> delete still offered on the 5, gated
- test/acts.test.ts: every act x every table, offer <=> accept, printed count == changed count

## Expected impact
No dossier button promises work its action will not do, and the reversible step no longer locks out the irreversible one. A new availability rule then has one home, as in hirelane.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the offer set and the accept set of every dossier act are one predicate
Before: 0 of 5 non-guard acceptance cases pass (probe on the fresh seed: tidy overclaims on 46/46 tables, 800 labelled vs 78 planned; BLK-05 staleIds 5 -> 0 after flagging)
After: 7 of 7
Method: gate - the acceptance cases in test/acts.test.ts
Result: better
Gate: none

Gate.tsx:76 `disabled={pending || table.ids.length === 0}`; Gate.tsx:81 `Tidy whitespace and email case · {table.ids.length} rows`; Gate.tsx:170 `disabled={table.staleIds.length === 0}`; lib/blocks/index.ts:176 `.filter((c) => c.is_stale === 1 && c.stale_flagged === 0)`; lib/mutations.ts:421 `getContacts(cap(ids)).filter((c) => c.deleted_at === null)`.

cards.title: The fourth check gets its repair: settle a company spelling in the dossier
shared_surfaces: examples/tidycrm/components/blocks/style/ (tidycrm-style) only if bk-chip[aria-pressed], bk-table and bk-truncated, which already exist, do not cover the preview
acceptance: settleState(table) for a table with spellings.length < 2 -> {kind:'none'}: no chooser, no act (guard: the Checks band already hides spellings then)
settleState for a conflicted table -> chooser lists every spelling, consensus first, nothing pre-selected (choosing which spelling is the company's real name is the person's decision, not the data's)

reduce(choose(spelling)) -> {kind:'previewing', spelling}; reduce(previewed(plan)) -> {kind:'ready', plan} whose act label reads 'File {plan.rewrites} contacts under "{spelling}"'; reduce(previewed(string)) -> {kind:'refused', reason}

on the 4 seeded conflicted tables where whitespace variants exist, the count the ready act prints is planCompany's rewrites, not records - n (the naive figure is wrong on 4 of 10 conflicted tables) -> equals resolveCompany's reported count
a stale preview cannot fire: choose A, choose B, then A's preview lands -> state stays previewing B (the act is never offered against a plan for a spelling the person moved off)
after the ready act runs resolveCompany(domain, spelling) and the sheet is rebuilt -> the table carries no conflict deviation, spellings.length === 1, and settleState returns {kind:'none'}
undoWrite(the resolve_company activity id) -> buildSheet restores the original spellings and the conflict deviation (guard: the AUTO band's undo promise holds for the new act)
premise: examples/tidycrm/components/blocks/dossier/Checks.tsx:46 - competing spellings print as inert spans; the conflict check is reported, not actionable
examples/tidycrm/components/blocks/dossier/Gate.tsx:60 - the AUTO bar repairs phone, whitespace, stale and pairs: three of the four checks have a repair here, conflict has none

examples/tidycrm/components/shell/HostCapabilities.tsx:357 - resolve_company exists and is AUTO, but only an agent can reach it; app/actions.ts:135 and :143 already expose preview and write to the client

examples/tidycrm/lib/mutations.ts:265 - planCompany rewrites `c.company !== canonical` (untrimmed), while lib/db.ts:385 groups spellings by TRIM(company): the dossier cannot compute the true count itself, so it has to ask the preview
examples/tidycrm/lib/mutations.ts:295 - resolveCompany logs `reversible: true` with a normalize undo, so the act belongs in the AUTO zone by the class rule
cards.rollback: Revert the series: settle.ts, Settle.tsx and the test go, Checks.tsx returns its spans, Gate.tsx loses the one AUTO control. No server action, mutation, schema or tool changes.

cards.runner_up: ADR 0111 parity for tidycrm: AUTO writes return undoId (lib/mutations.ts), the toast carries Undo through the kit's existing ToastAction, and the dossier shows a receipt for the last act. Today the AUTO band promises undo and no surface calls undoAction.
cards.body:
## Summary
The dossier lists four checks. For three of them the AUTO bar has a repair. For the company-spelling conflict, on 10 of the 46 tables, it prints the competing spellings and offers nothing. The resolve_company write already exists, is reversible and is AUTO, but only an agent can reach it. The change: make the spellings a chooser, preview the rewrite, and offer one AUTO act that files the domain under the chosen spelling.

## Description
`dossier/settle.ts` is a pure state machine: none | choosing | previewing(spelling) | ready(plan) | refused(reason). Each preview carries the spelling it was asked for, so a late answer for an abandoned choice is dropped. `Checks.tsx` turns the spelling spans into an aria-pressed chip group, with nothing pre-selected, because which spelling is the company's real name is the person's decision. `Settle.tsx` shows previewCompanyAction's rewrites and its bounded sample of changes, `(showing N of M)` included. `Gate.tsx` gains one AUTO control, 'File N contacts under "X"', run through the existing useRun. The control keeps ADR 0022's two zones, and arming still takes the bar. The count comes from the preview because the naive records - n is wrong on 4 of 10 conflicted tables (whitespace variants). This is registry technique hitl-approval/oracle-before-gate: the person sees what the write will change before it runs.

## Flow
- open a conflicted table -> Checks band shows the spellings as a chooser
- pick one -> previewCompanyAction -> 'rewrites 7 of 15: sample...'
- AUTO bar: 'File 7 contacts under "Pinegrove Collective"' -> resolveCompanyAction -> toast -> sheet revalidates -> conflict check turns to a pass
- undo is unchanged: the activity row is reversible and the agent's undo or a later receipt puts it back

## Expected impact
A person can clear every check the dossier prints without leaving it or asking an agent, and sees the true rewrite before committing.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - every check the dossier reports has a repair it can run, previewed
Before: 0 of 5 non-guard acceptance cases pass (no settle module; the dossier has no path to resolveCompany; naive count wrong on 4/10 conflicted tables by probe)
After: 7 of 7
Method: gate - the acceptance cases in test/settle.test.ts (pure reducer plus real planCompany/resolveCompany/undoWrite in a temp home)
Result: better
Gate: none
